rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 - the authors train and test their own LSTM/GRU/BLSTM/CNN/MLP/RF models on climate data and AquaCrop-simulated yields for a site in Portugal (Tables 4, 8).
rows.notes: The study builds a yield-prediction model (BLSTM) using climate data, irrigation amount and soil water content as inputs; it does not implement or test a precision irrigation scheduling system and reports no water-use reduction (no 30% figure, no comparison with traditional irrigation). The only irrigation 'application' (Section 3, Algorithm 1, Table 10) uses random irrigation amounts to compute a hypothetical net return; the authors state a reinforcement-learning scheduler is future work. Yield data are AquaCrop simulations never compared with field measurements. Supports at most a precondition (a yield predictor that could become part of a decision system).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 - own deep learning model runs trained/tested on climate and AquaCrop-simulated tomato and potato yield data (Tables 4, 8, Figure 10).
rows.notes: The study shows that BLSTM can predict end-of-season tomato and potato yield (R2 0.97-0.99 on test set) from climate, irrigation and soil water inputs. It does not test whether a precision irrigation system maintains or improves yield; no scheduling system is evaluated against conventional irrigation, and yields are simulated (AquaCrop), not measured. The yield model is proposed as a component of a future decision-support system (precondition only).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2, 3 - own model runs: BLSTM trained on 45 and tested on 20 potato seasons simulated with AquaCrop under different irrigation depths (Table 8, Figure 10).
rows.notes: No 15% potato yield increase is reported, and no quality (size, weight, grade) or water-stress outcome is measured. The study only reports prediction accuracy of a potato yield model (MSE 0.039, R2 0.988) on AquaCrop-simulated data; it does not operate a machine-learning irrigation scheduler adjusting water from real-time weather and soil moisture and compare resulting yields. Inputs are historical station data and simulated soil water, not real-time sensors. Supports only a precondition of the claimed effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 - own deep learning model runs on climate and AquaCrop-simulated yield data.
rows.notes: The study contains nothing on disease, waterlogging or soil aeration; it is a yield-prediction modelling study. No own evidence on the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a modelling paper: deep learning yield predictors trained on 10 years of weather-station data and AquaCrop-simulated yields/soil water for sandy loam at Fadagosa, Portugal; sprinkler irrigation in the simulations. No precision irrigation scheduling system is implemented or compared with conventional irrigation; reinforcement-learning scheduling is explicitly future work. The reviews' figures (30% water saving, 15% potato yield increase, disease reduction) do not appear in the study.
